# `Q-5-29` — Declared Stylesheet Not Found

> A `css:` entry names a stylesheet that does not exist, so it was
> not copied into the output. Every page linking it will request a
> file that is not there. The render continues; the (broken) link is
> still emitted.

## What this means

A document or project can attach extra stylesheets to its HTML
output with the `css` option:

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
format:
  html:
    css:
      - styles.css
```

Quarto resolves each entry **relative to the file that declares
it**: entries in `_quarto.yml` resolve against the project root,
entries in a directory's `_metadata.yml` against that directory, and
entries in a document's front matter against the document's own
directory. A leading `/` anchors the path at the project root from
any of those places.

When the resolved file exists, Quarto copies it into the output
tree and emits a depth-correct `<link>` on every page. This warning
fires when the file does **not** exist: nothing is copied, and the
`<link>` is emitted with the path exactly as you wrote it — visibly
broken in the browser's network tab rather than silently absent.

## Common causes

- **A typo in the path**, or a file that was moved or renamed
  without updating the `css` entry.
- **A path written relative to the wrong anchor** — for example, a
  document in `posts/2026/` declaring `css: styles.css` for a file
  that actually lives at the project root. From front matter that
  entry names `posts/2026/styles.css`; write `/styles.css` (or
  `../../styles.css`) instead.
- **A stylesheet that is generated later** by a tool that has not
  run yet.

## How to fix it

Check the path in the `css` entry against the anchor of the file
that declares it, or add the missing stylesheet. If the stylesheet
belongs to the project as a whole, declaring it once in
`_quarto.yml` (project-root-relative) is usually clearer than
repeating it per document.
